contract: Explicit Run source variant retaining guarded lifecycle, children, completion and Run-owned dispatch, plus release_approved committing or currently revalidating exact-action Approval without intent admission, activation, work scheduling or send, and renew/2 renewing the held lease between commands, installing only its own next-revision token and stopping on a fenced, lost or unknown renewal, with status/2 reporting renewed_since, the revision of the latest committed stream record that is not a lease renewal, rebuilt at startup; Resource retains its independent current lifetime/FIFO and reservation-before-send boundary.
limits: One live Run stream uses either this owner or old Run, never both; no migration, handoff, engine, descriptor registry, transferable permission or cross-stream release/dispatch transaction.
Release alone does not establish no prior send or provider completion. Retained dispatch_approved still sends; trusted callers select one dispatch owner and serialize cancellation/admission.

Host supplies fresh authenticated evidence/authority, exact descriptor correlation, durable Store, clocks, exclusive ownership, retention, outstanding-write confirmation and physical fencing before replacement/activation.

Whole guarded history retained; no aggregate history/memory bound. Individual events at most128KiB, Run identifiers at most200 UTF-8 bytes without NUL, provider refs at most64; ready Approval/EffectIntent bounds unchanged.
Finite PostgreSQL, Memory and fake-Adapter scenarios, not universal proofs or production monitoring. Memory is volatile; uncertain writes/caller timeouts require reconciliation, not resend.

Child death is best effort: no pid is stored, so a death is not recorded when the owner restarts before or while the child ends, or when its write is fenced or rejected; a death whose write failed with an error is kept in the process and written after the next command.

A renewal changes the held revision that status/2 reports without any Run transition; renewed_since tells renewals apart only as this owner holds the stream (as revision): every Run of the owner reports the same value, a command of any of them moves it, and it says nothing about rows that another writer appended.

grounding.claim: Nine copied Run groups plus Release without dispatch, Waiting and retained consent, Release restart windows, Currentness and authority change, Resource-owned send and Isolation, copy and checked example exercise renamed bytes with real ready owners/disposable PostgreSQL, call tracing and counting fake Adapter; actual production commit/revalidation mutations are negative controls. Groups missing_evidence_is_refused, failed_death_write_is_kept and death_is_best_effort are finite cases; mutations of the stored-evidence condition and of the kept deaths are negative controls. Group lease_renewal (ELZ-422) renews on PostgreSQL (writes after renewal, the expected-revision floor across Run, child and death writes, another writer and an owner restart, a lease lost to a claimant and to expiry, a renewal outside the owner, an indeterminate renewal after commit with its receipt, a malformed renewal reply after commit, definite no-write errors, commands after status reads while another process renews, one with a coordinated renewal between read and command) and on the Memory Lease double (an append committed before its backend is killed: unknown without a receipt); a mutation that keeps the old token fails the write-after-renewal case with {:refused, :conflict}, and a mutation that reads the token without checking its fields fails the malformed-reply case. Group renewed_since (ELZ-429) shows on PostgreSQL that status/2 reports the latest revision that is not a renewal, kept across renewals and moved by Run, child and death writes, and that a new owner rebuilds it from the stream (the record before renewals for a replacement, the claim after a release and a claim, the seize after a seize); mutations that set it from the startup floor or count Run records only fail its cases.

Pinned GenServer serialization, monitoring and task semantics, not a local runtime proof. Source variant copies Run at repository baseline2b3c3fc763eb8eef0d4d4cfbe694098ea83de217; README names copied paths.
OTP29.1.2 safe canonical ETF and crypto digests; existing ready Approval laws and Store/Lease/EffectIntent/RunResource Contracts remain unchanged, not a new shell persistence proof.

Host authenticates identities/evidence/current context and settlement, retains exact action-to-descriptor correlation, serializes currentness/cancellation/dispatch, supplies durable Store/clocks/supervision/full history and fences outstanding writes/old owners/providers before activation. Host renews through renew/2 before the lease until and, after a stopped renewal, confirms its receipt or, without one, backend and predecessor fencing and the durable head before a replacement. Test host grants and observations are simulations, not production fencing evidence.

telemetry.contract: OTP diagnostics only; consumer redacts. No custom payload events or exporter.

config.contract: Retained construction-time Store/held Lease/effect_intent bindings; map may be empty for release-only. No new option, defaults or hot configuration.

control.contract: Retained trusted Run commands plus release_approved; released means durable current Approval, waiting grants no work, neither activates/admit/schedules/sends. Status and old released replies grant no current dispatch authority. renew/2 renews the held lease between commands: it installs only a token at the held revision + 1, keeps its token on a definite no-write error and stops on a fenced, lost, indeterminate or unknown renewal; commands accept an expected revision separated from the current one solely by renewals this live owner installed. status/2 reports renewed_since, the revision of the latest committed stream record whose kind is not lease_renewed, rebuilt from the stream at startup and moved by every successful Run append.
